claims.title: CC0 Halloween: The Cursed Loot (4-Panel Comic)
claims.description:
🎃 **"The Cursed Loot"** — A 4-panel CC0 Halloween Comic Strip.

### The Story
On Halloween night, Pip—an intrepid Noun sporting signature red Noggles—is out trick-or-treating in a foggy gothic churchyard. He wanders across an ancient stone crypt where a shadowy, violet-eyed specter rises from the mist to offer him legendary power: the mythical **Cursed Blade of Torment** from the Loot contract. Pip checks that it's public domain, claims it with a grin, and marvels at its balance. But when midnight strikes, the true curse is unleashed: the sword awakens with animated eyes, a manic grin, and the relentless, booming energy of a 24/7 fitness influencer.

### Panel Breakdown
- **Panel 1 (The Encounter)**: A foggy moonlit cemetery. A shadowy ghost looms from the crypt: *"Mortal! You dare enter the Crypt on Halloween night?!"* Pip, chewing on candy: *"Just trick-or-treating. Nice fog."*
- **Panel 2 (The Offer)**: The ghost dramatically presents a crackling runic blade on an altar: *"Take this Cursed Blade of Torment! But beware... whosoever claims it is bound to its eternal, maddening curse!"* Pip asks: *"Is it CC0 Loot? Public domain?"* Ghost: *"Yes, free to claim!"*
- **Panel 3 (The Claim)**: Pip tests the blade's swing with an easy smile: *"Feels well-balanced! I don't feel any curse?"* The ghost smirks sinisterly: *"Just wait for midnight..."*
- **Panel 4 (The Twist)**: Midnight strikes! The blade springs to life with cartoon eyes and a cheerful grin, shouting musical motivational chatter: *"GM! RISE AND GRIND! TIME FOR 50 BURPEES AND POSITIVE VIBES! LET'S GOOO!"* Pip covers his ears in pure agony: *"NOOO! MAKE IT STOP! TAKE IT BACK!"* The ghost backs away cackling: *"No refunds! Eternal torment!"*

---

Every character and item in this comic is 100% public domain / CC0:
- **Noun Character (Pip)**: Distinctive square red glasses (Noggles) from the **Nouns DAO** collection ([nouns.wtf](https://nouns.wtf/brand), CC0).

claims.title: The Last Guest
claims.description:
On Halloween night, Runner #8417 finds an invitation glowing above the entrance of an abandoned building: “One guest remaining.” Inside, the halls are empty, the candles are still burning, and an open guestbook is waiting at the reception desk. The Runner’s name is already written on its final page.

Then an old television flickers to life. It shows the building’s entrance, the same invitation, the same empty street. And there, on the screen, is Runner #8417, making the exact movements they made moments ago.

The Runner steps closer. The figure on the screen does the same. The television displays a message: “Please remain until checkout.”

Something is wrong. The building is not only watching. It remembers.

The Runner looks back at the guestbook. Beside their name, a new word sits: “RETURNING.”

The television switches back to the entrance. Another Runner #8417 is approaching the door.

Inside, the first one has not moved.

The invitation still reads, “One guest remaining.”

Trick or Treat (and Proof) — a four-panel CC0 Halloween comic

Image proof (single image, four panels): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/9xj89gzrtw-hue/poidh-1500-cc0-halloween/refs/heads/main/comic.png

The comic:

Panel 1 — Night street, lit window, pumpkin bucket. A kid with a phone says: "Pics or it
didn't happen." The ghost answers: "…what?"

Panel 2 — The ghost goes full haunted-house: arms up, mouth open, "BOOOOO." The kid, unimpressed,
still filming: "Cool. Where's the proof, though?"

Panel 3 — The ghost gives up and leans in for the selfie. "Fine. A selfie." The kid: "Say cheese."

Panel 4 — The photo. The kid is in it, the pumpkin is in it, the ghost is not: only an empty
dashed outline where it stood, and a translucent ghost pressed against the edge of the frame with
one tear. Caption: "Third Halloween. Still no proof I was there."

The joke flips the platform's own slogan. "Pics or it didn't happen" is easy to say and brutal if
you are the thing that does not develop on film: the ghost has the scariest costume and the worst
camera presence, so the burden of proof lands on the one creature that can never meet it.
